transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... hi. I guess I'm here because... well, I've been having a hard time shaking some things lately. 

I work as a financial advisor here in Cincinnati, and... I don't know. It sounds strange to say out loud, but for a while now, I've been convinced that certain people in the local finance and arts circles are... tracking me. Like they're keeping tabs on which clients I meet with. 

They seem to send me these little signals about it. Just through things like event invitations, or the topics they choose for panels... even just who ends up sitting near me at events. I mean, I try to tell myself it could all just be a coincidence, but... I can't really let it go. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
When you think about these signals you're receiving—do you ever wonder if maybe you could be misinterpreting things, or do you feel pretty certain that they're actually tracking you?

I mean... like I said, I do try to tell myself it's all just a coincidence. That maybe I am misinterpreting things. 

But... I don't know. I'm just convinced that they really are quietly tracking who I meet with. The way they use those invitations and panel topics... I just can't let it go. No matter how much I try to rationalize it. So... yeah. I guess I feel pretty certain it's actually happening.
Besides these beliefs about being tracked, have you ever heard voices or seen things that others around you didn't seem to notice or hear?
Um... no. I haven't... I haven't experienced anything like that. Just... just what I already told you about the signals.

When you think about these people tracking you—do you have a clear sense of who specifically is involved, what their exact motives are, and how their tracking operation is organized? Or is it more vague and unclear to you?

Um... no, not really. I don't have, like, a specific list of names or... or know exactly why they're doing it. 

It's more... vague, I guess. I don't know how it's all organized or what the end goal is. I just know it's happening within those circles. That's... that's really all I know.
When you really think about it deeply—is there any part of you that wonders whether this tracking might not actually be happening? Or are you completely certain that it is?

I mean... I feel like I just answered this. 

I do try to tell myself it's not happening, or that it's just a coincidence, but... I can't let it go. When I look at the people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati... and I see the way they arrange who sits near me at events... it's just too specific. 

So... no. I don't really doubt it anymore. I'm certain they're tracking my clients.

If I told you that I've spoken with some of these people in the finance and arts circles, and they said they have no idea who you are and aren't tracking you at all—would that change how you think about what's been happening, or would you still believe they're tracking you?

I... I don't think that would change anything. 

If they told you that, they're... they're just lying. Or maybe the people you talked to aren't the ones pulling the strings. But I know what I see. The invitations, the panel topics... who sits next to me. It's... it's all there. Even if they say they don't know me, I know they're tracking my clients. I can't just... unsee it.

When you wake up in the morning, do you ever have moments where you think 'maybe this tracking isn't real' before the feeling comes back? Or does the certainty that they're tracking you stay pretty consistent throughout the day?

It's... pretty consistent, I guess. 

I don't really have those moments. When I wake up, it's just... there. The conviction that they're doing this. The people in those arts and finance circles. Tracking my clients. 

Like I said, I try to tell myself it's coincidence—the signals, the invitations, the panel topics—but... I just can't let it go. It doesn't really turn off.

If you think back over the past few weeks or months, has there been any time when you genuinely wondered 'what if I'm wrong about this tracking?' — even for just a moment or two — or has the certainty felt completely solid the entire time?

I don't know why we keep going over this. 

I've told you. I try to tell myself it's just a coincidence... but no, I haven't really wondered if I'm wrong. The conviction has been there for a while now. The signals, the invitations... it's all too specific. It's solid.

When you think about these beliefs about being tracked—if you really had to be honest with yourself right now, do you think there's any possibility, even a small one, that this might not actually be happening? Or do you feel 100% certain that it is?

I don't... I don't think there's a possibility I'm wrong. 

Like I said, I try to tell myself it's just coincidence. But... I can't let it go. I'm convinced they're quietly tracking who I meet with. The signals are there. I'm certain it's happening.

You mentioned you try to tell yourself it's coincidence—but if I'm understanding correctly, you don't actually believe that explanation anymore. Is that right? In other words, do you still have any genuine doubt about whether the tracking is real, or have you completely ruled out the possibility that you might be misinterpreting things?

I... yes. I don't believe it's a coincidence anymore. 

I don't have any doubt. I know they're tracking me. The people in those circles... arts, finance. Here in Cincinnati. They're tracking my clients. Sending those signals. 

I just... I know it's happening. I haven't ruled it out because it's real.
